task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 (implement fix) for GH-716 / ISS-0675. CODE-DESIGNER Step 2 (this run) returned SKIPPED with a full verified rationale (see that handoff's result.summary) confirming this is a pure code-deletion task with zero live callers and zero design risk. Implement exactly the confirmed deletion:

1. In src/event_store/store.zig, DELETE:
   - Store.reconstructBounded() (public method, ~line 1259-1353) including its doc comment block (~line 1233-1258, the 'reconstructBounded (PAR-06 AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6)' section header comment) -- note the doc comment contains a STALE/INACCURATE claim that reconstruction.zig 'is this store method's caller'; this is being removed, not corrected, since the whole function goes.
   - lookupOrRepairEventWindowInternal() private helper (~line 1355-1457)
   - mergeEventRowsBySequence() private helper (~line 1662-1710)
   - rowSequenceNumber() private helper (~line 1712-1720)
   - The EventWindow struct (~line 205) IF it is only used by the deleted functions (verify via grep -n "EventWindow" src/event_store/store.zig after removing the above -- if zero remaining references, delete the struct too)
   - StoreError.ReconstructionWindowMissing and StoreError.UnboundedReconstructionRefused variants from the StoreError error set (~line 87, ~line 93) and their doc comments -- confirmed by CODE-DESIGNER to have zero live return sites and zero exhaustive-switch dependents once the dead helper is removed (retentionPolicyErrorCode()'s switch at ~line 1737 is non-exhaustive with an else catch-all and does not name either variant)
2. Clean up stale references to the deleted function found during design verification:
   - src/engine/instance.zig:83's comment mentions 'reconstructBounded()'s exclusive `<` comparison' as a numeric-convention reference -- reword it to describe the convention without naming the now-deleted function (e.g. reference reconstruction.zig's eventWindowForInstanceInTx()/reconstructInstance() bounded-query convention instead, since that is the still-live code establishing the same convention)
   - src/design/par-06-time-bounded-reconstruction.md: this is a historical design document: do NOT rewrite its Open Questions section rationale (that's the accurate historical record of the ambiguity that caused this dead code), but DO add a brief note/addendum (e.g. a short 'Resolution (GH-716)' section) stating the ambiguity was resolved by deleting Store.reconstructBounded() and keeping reconstruction.zig as sole entry point, with a pointer to ISS-0675/GH-716
   - tests/integration/par06_reconstruction_bounded_test.zig's file header (~line 7-12) currently describes Store.reconstructBounded() as 'DEAD CODE' in present tense; update it to past tense noting it WAS dead code and has now been removed (GH-716), since the function will no longer exist to describe
   - tests/specs/PAR-06.md (~line 37-48): same treatment -- update present-tense 'is DEAD CODE'/'unreferenced' language to past tense noting removal via GH-716, if still accurate to leave the historical context
   - src/event_store/store.zig:1713's comment 'reconstructBounded() query branches share' on rowSequenceNumber() is being deleted along with rowSequenceNumber() itself, so no action needed there

3. Verify the codebase still compiles: `zig build` (or the project's standard build command) exits 0.
4. Verify existing tests still pass: `zig build test-integration-par06` and `zig build test-integration-par06-reconstruction` both exit 0 -- these should be UNAFFECTED by this change since they already exercise only the live reconstruction.zig path (per the test file's own header, confirmed by ISSUE-FIXER).
5. Run the full unit test suite (`zig build test` or the project's equivalent) and confirm no regressions.
6. Update docs/issues/ISS-0675.json: set status to RESOLVED, fill in `resolution` (what was deleted, why, evidence tests still pass), `verification` (which tests were run and passed), `files_changed` (list every file touched), and `resolved_at` (real timestamp via python tools/utcnow.py).
7. Commit the changes on this branch (feature/WF03-GH716-20260812) with a clear commit message referencing GH-716/ISS-0675/PAR-06. Do NOT push yet -- push happens at Step Final.

Do NOT touch any other PAR-06 acceptance criteria or unrelated code. Do NOT modify reconstruction.zig's actual logic (it is already correct and is the surviving implementation) -- only the stale comment noted above in instance.zig, and no behavioral changes to reconstruction.zig itself.
